target_customer: Small and mid-sized US businesses buying commercial insurance (daycares, manufacturers, dealerships, restaurants)
problem: Buying commercial insurance through traditional brokers is slow and manual; Harper automates forms, carrier matching and client communication.
business_model: Insurance brokerage earning carrier commissions, with an AI workflow platform (Harper Hub)

founders.name: Tushar Nair
founders.background_notes: Education not listed on YC page.

competitors.name: 1Fort
competitors.what: AI-driven specialty insurance marketplace for independent brokers

competitors.name: Outmarket AI
competitors.what: Intelligence layer for brokers, MGAs and carriers

technical_complexity.rationale: LLM automation of forms and carrier matching is standard engineering; the hard part is licensing and carrier integrations across states.

defensibility.rationale: Broker licensing, carrier relationships (160+ carriers per TechCrunch) and customer renewals create stickiness, but AI tooling is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response found; many AI broker startups launched 2024 to 2026.

market_need_then: Commercial insurance for small businesses is slow and phone based; the founder's family brokerage gave direct insight. YC page reports over $6M annualized premiums by the batch.

branding.name_origin: Named after Dakotah Rice's mother's maiden name (TechCrunch and a BusinessWire based republication).

brand_strength.rationale: Human, easy name but common word; no press on the brand itself beyond the origin story.

outcome_analysis: Harper grew from a Winter 2025 batch company to over 5,000 customers and a $46.8M seed and Series A led by Emergence Capital in February 2026. Family insurance experience, fast customer acquisition and the AI timing wave helped. Risks are crowded AI broker competition and commission economics. No exit has occurred.
notes: Seed of March 2025 from Pioneer Fund appears only in an aggregator with undisclosed amount, kept as a round with null amount. Reporters list different co-investors (Antler, 10X Founders and others in one report). Co-founder Tushar Nair is described by TechCrunch as friend and former Poolit CTO.
